title: IXDE carried by one kind, the prey of c52's digestion ecology: free condensate bodies that eat fuel, divide to generation 5 and 3 on two fresh 256^2 seeds only when predators are present (twins frozen), and each dissolve within 200 t when the fuel supply is cut around that one body while their neighbours and the matter stay
summary: Reviewers of 20261027T0325-c52-digestion-ecology-claim doubted that the predators are individuals (my 20261027T0828-c56-free-predator-test: free predators dissolve, none of 47 divisions has a free parent). This claim tests the other kind of the same world, unchanged (c52's world.py, defaults), for all four capabilities. Labkit, 256^2, t=12000, default window K=20, fresh seeds 7 and 8: prey 82 and 94 persistent tracks, 62 and 63 persistent splits, generation 5 and 3, merge/split 0.40 and 0.41. Matched predator-free twins (same seeds, grid, duration, window): 149 and 147 static prey, 0 persistent splits, 1 moving track each. Global fuel cut at t=6000 (128^2, seeds 7 and 8, labkit) against fed twins: prey 42 -> 3 -> 0 and 47 -> 1 -> 0 within 200 t (fed 42-47), mean prey material 0.284 -> 0.291 and 0.286 -> 0.293 (kept). Local fuel cut (fuel regrowth kF set to 0 in a disk of radius 12 around one prey body at t=6000, two bodies per seed): each targeted prey (area 49-63) is gone by t=6200 in all 4 cuts, while the same body in the fed twin keeps 22-77 px to t=8000 and the prey bodies more than 27 px from the cut are as many as in the fed twin.

claims.statement: In pack/seed7 and pack/seed8 (python -m labkit.run <c52 world.py> --seeds <s> --size 256 256 --frames 120 --no-movie, defaults, K=20) prey condensates form from noise as separate bodies of a conserved material that condenses only up its own catalysis product of a consumed, regrowing fuel; with the predators present they divide repeatedly (62 and 63 persistent splits, generation 5 and 3) and move (318 and 307 moving tracks), where the matched predator-free twins are frozen (0 persistent splits, 1 moving track); each prey body depends on its own fuel supply: a local cut of fuel regrowth around one body dissolves it within 200 t while its neighbours stay, and a global cut dissolves every prey with the prey material kept.
claims.track: seed 7, prey track 58 -> 185 -> 381 -> 443 -> 499 -> 556 -> 629 (pack/seed7/prey_ancestry_s7.png, .json): nucleates from noise, divides at t=5300, 6200, 7400, 8600 and 9800 (generation 5) and is alive at t=12000; every division is a predator cutting through it. The same-kind bodies cut in lcut/ (seed 7: the prey at (76,72) and (19,71); seed 8: (62,65) and (33,27) at t=6000) dissolve when their own fuel is cut

controls_run.X: twin/seed7 and twin/seed8 (pred_on 0, same seeds, grid, duration and window): prey 149 and 147 static bodies, 0 persistent splits, generation 0, 1 moving track; with predators prey 172 and 173 bodies on average, 62 and 63 persistent splits, 318 and 307 moving tracks. Sign: predators raise prey number, division and motion (they cut prey while eating them); predators need prey (c52's dfork, and my 20261027T0828-c56-free-predator-test)
controls_run.E: fork/ffork128_s7 and _s8 (fork_t 6000: F set to 0, regrowth off) against fork/fed128_s7 and _s8 (fuelfork.json): prey 42 -> 0 and 47 -> 0 by t=6200, fed 42-47; mean prey material kept. Per individual: lcut/lcut_s7a, s7b, s8a, s8b (cut_t 6000, cut_r 12 around one prey body) against the fed twins: the cut body 60/49/63/51 px -> 0 by t=6200 in all 4; the fed body 22/30/77/39 px at t=8000; bodies far from the cut 41/39/38/35 vs 42/40/39/41 at t=8000

limits: Prey division in this world is driven by the predators: every strict prey division (27 and 34, splits3.py at area >= 30) has a predator within 6 px, the predator cuts through the prey body (strict_prey_s7.png, prey_ancestry), and the twins never divide; a reviewer may weigh this as division imposed by the other kind. Daughters start at half the parent's area and are not larger 1000 t later (regrow.py: median 0.45 and 0.53 of the parent on seeds 7 and 8), the same as spontaneous divisions of c46's prey in its predator-free twin (0.49). 92% of prey bodies touch a predator in a frame (prey_free.json, gap <= 2 px). The prey's condensed state needs the product p, which lives ~1 t, so the fuel cuts remove prey within 1-2 frames: the dependence is immediate, not a slow starvation. Fuel diffuses (DF 10) into the local-cut disk, so the local cut lowers rather than removes the body's supply. Forks and local cuts at 128^2; one parameter point; no dt/2 or grid variant of my own (c52 reports dt/2 and 1.5x grid checks of the same world); no Laplacian-only twin. The predators of this world are not claimed here (they are attached to prey; see 20261027T0828-c56-free-predator-test).
